raw_case_text: A 22-year-old female patient arrived at the emergency room presenting with generalized seizures, which had been preceded by a week of headaches. On examination using a head CT scan, an intracerebral cyst of middle size (2.3 x 2.1 x 3 cm) was identified in the right frontal lobe [Figure 4]. The cyst exhibited a calcified nodule and was accompanied by brain edema in the surrounding area. Considering these findings, the patient was promptly taken to the operating room for further evaluation and treatment, with a probable diagnosis of an oligodendroglioma tumor.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with generalized seizures preceded by a 1-week history of headaches.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced 1 week of headaches before developing generalized seizures that prompted emergency room presentation.

objective.advanced_workup: Head CT scan identified a medium-sized intracerebral cyst measuring 2.3 x 2.1 x 3 cm in the right frontal lobe containing a calcified nodule and surrounded by perilesional brain edema.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Based on the right frontal cystic lesion with a calcified nodule and surrounding edema on head CT, the patient was taken promptly to the operating room for surgical evaluation and resection under a probable preoperative diagnosis of an oligodendroglioma tumor.
